There's only so many games I can think of that translated well into a whole new genre, my fondest memory being with [B]Commandos: Strike Force[/B]: it kept everything the series was popular for, still being fun to play, even though it wasn't the same at its core (hardcore fans would probably disagree with me, but any die-hard FPS enthusiast will most likely find a gem here). The Warhammer series offers a total of 4 first-person shooter adaptions, [B]Space Hulk: Deathwing[/B], [B]Warhammer 40,000: Fire Warrior[/B], and [B]Warhammer: End Times - Vermintide 1 & 2[/B], but they were not made by Relic Entertainment. Unlike Space Marine. The team putting all their life into strategy games suddenly got the idea to compete with Gears of War and similar titles. An attempt to broaden the audience? 

Let's get right to the point here: the game blows. It's not bad by unplayable standards, but it offers nothing original or interesting. You'd think with a universe as vast as Warhammer, they'd try harder to explore its strengths and implement them in story delivery as well as gameplay mechanics. But nope, what we got is a campaign with boring characters and extremely predictable turns, all taking place in mostly sterile and repetitive environments. The voice cast is good, but the lack of facial animations are part of technical limitations. What I can definitely give credit for is the detailed armor / enemy design that fans love the franchise so much for and some of the locations in the distance are a sight to behold. But there's just not enough. Not enough of anything, in fact.

 How does gameplay fare against the traditional TPS action? It's a mix of hack & slay and ordinary shooting elements, heavily underdeveloped, but backed up by a serviceable arsenal, my favorites being the Storm Bolter and the Thunder Hammer. Friendly AI is brain-dead, as you would expect them to be, the ammo placement doesn't always make sense, displaying furthermore how the developers aren't really versed in proper TPS design. Huge empty corridors, an elevator ride, enclosed empty corridors, another elevator ride, ugh... again, variety is this game's biggest minus, but when it DOES get fun with the jump-pack sections, it lasts 5 minutes max until you return to the same old. And why the hell is there no cover system? I mean, lack thereof doesn't make the game more challenging or longer, it's just that excluding it in an almost borderline copy of Gears is questionable. Then again, everything here feels rushed and unpolished anyway. And the final boss is a QTE topped off with a cliffhanger-ish ending, whooptie-fkin-doo.

With all the issues, Space Marine isn't only an inferior Gears, it's just lazy and barren, clearly a failed transition. Show some appreciation to underdogs such as [B]Inversion[/B] instead, now that's a clone done right!

I am really agreeably surprised.  I got it for free from Humble Bundle and I did not expect it to be so much fun and well done! 

The graphics and FPS are smooth and it is really fun to play : the various weapons you can use are all impactful and fun.  The melee is gory (and a bit necessary to use as melee hits gives you Fury which can heal you when you do an Execute move). 

For a 2011 game, my expectations were low, yet the visuals and animations are nice ! 

I am having a blast playing it !  Expect to die once in a while though on Normal difficulty (Warhammer 40K is a deadly world).

AMBIANCE / LORE (single-player campaign) : 
Humans are more endearing (sympathetic or humane) than in other Warhammer 40K stories, mostly because you meet ordinary Guards and hear reports from medics for example.  You are an Ultramarine (a rather elite Space Marine) and you help an Inquisitor secure a weapon away from Orks dirty hands. 

- campaign takes on average 9 hours 
(400+ players polled on the site Howlongtobeat...)

TECH TIPS :
- First, I did not crash once (!), which is actually rare for action games I find. 
- Made for Windows 7 : to launch it, you may need to run the .exe in Windows 7 Compatiblity mode (if you are using Windows 10).  The first time you launch it, you *might* also have to run it with the Steam Launch Option -window, but just setting the .exe to Windows 7 mode should be fine.

Story is not really flushed out, but its not really about the story. Game play is amazing! 9/10
The quintessential Warhammer 40k experience. It really makes you feel like an Astartes mowing trough hordes of greenskins.
This is and amazing game. A must for any 40k fan.
